From 6dccbc9f3e1d38565dff7730d2b7d1e8b16c9b09 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Peddolla Harshavardhan Reddy <peddolla.reddy@oss.qualcomm.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 21:36:59 +0530
Subject: [PATCH] wifi: cfg80211: cancel pmsr_free_wk in
 cfg80211_pmsr_wdev_down

When the nl80211 socket that originated a PMSR request is
closed, cfg80211_release_pmsr() sets the request's nl_portid
to zero and schedules pmsr_free_wk to process the abort
asynchronously. If the interface is concurrently torn down
before that work runs, cfg80211_pmsr_wdev_down() calls
cfg80211_pmsr_process_abort() directly. However, the already-
scheduled pmsr_free_wk work item remains pending and may run
after the interface has been removed from the driver. This
could cause the driver's abort_pmsr callback to operate on a
torn-down interface, leading to undefined behavior and
potential crashes.

Cancel pmsr_free_wk synchronously in cfg80211_pmsr_wdev_down()
before calling cfg80211_pmsr_process_abort(). This ensures any
pending or in-progress work is drained before interface teardown
proceeds, preventing the work from invoking the driver abort
callback after the interface is gone.

Fixes: 9bb7e0f24e7e ("cfg80211: add peer measurement with FTM initiator API")
Signed-off-by: Peddolla Harshavardhan Reddy <peddolla.reddy@oss.qualcomm.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260305160712.1263829-3-peddolla.reddy@oss.qualcomm.com
Signed-off-by: Johannes Berg <johannes.berg@intel.com>

diff --git a/net/wireless/pmsr.c b/net/wireless/pmsr.c
index 44bd88c9ea66..50e8e19aa366 100644
--- a/net/wireless/pmsr.c
+++ b/net/wireless/pmsr.c
@@ -664,6 +664,7 @@ void cfg80211_pmsr_wdev_down(struct wireless_dev *wdev)
 	}
 	spin_unlock_bh(&wdev->pmsr_lock);
 
+	cancel_work_sync(&wdev->pmsr_free_wk);
 	if (found)
 		cfg80211_pmsr_process_abort(wdev);
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of the Patch

### Files Modified

**net/wireless/pmsr.c**  
- Added a call to `cancel_work_sync(&wdev->pmsr_free_wk)` inside `cfg80211_pmsr_wdev_down()`, placed right before the call to `cfg80211_pmsr_process_abort()` when a pending PMSR request is found.

### Relationship Between Changes

The modification addresses a race condition during interface teardown. When an nl80211 socket that initiated a PMSR request is closed, the system sets the request's `nl_portid` to zero and schedules the work item `pmsr_free_wk` to abort the measurement asynchronously. If the wireless device (wdev) is brought down *before* that work runs, `cfg80211_pmsr_wdev_down()` directly calls `cfg80211_pmsr_process_abort()`. However, the previously scheduled work item remained pending and could execute later, after the interface was already removed from the driver. This could lead to the driver's `abort_pmsr` callback operating on a torn-down interface, causing undefined behavior or crashes.

By inserting `cancel_work_sync(&wdev->pmsr_free_wk)`, the patch ensures that any pending or currently executing `pmsr_free_wk` work is fully drained before the abort process is triggered. This guarantees that the driver abort callback will only be invoked while the interface is still valid, preventing the race condition. The fix is minimal and directly targets the root cause by synchronously canceling the scheduled work at the point where the device is being torn down.

Fixes: 9bb7e0f24e7e ("cfg80211: add peer measurement with FTM initiator API")
Signed-off-by: Peddolla Harshavardhan Reddy <peddolla.reddy@oss.qualcomm.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260305160712.1263829-3-peddolla.reddy@oss.qualcomm.com
Signed-off-by: Johannes Berg <johannes.berg@intel.com>

Here is the root cause:
In cfg80211_pmsr_wdev_down(), the pmsr_free_wk work item, which was scheduled asynchronously by cfg80211_release_pmsr() when an nl80211 socket is closed, is not canceled before calling cfg80211_pmsr_process_abort(). This allows the work to potentially execute after the interface has been torn down, causing the driver's abort_pmsr callback to operate on an invalid interface, leading to undefined behavior or crashes.

Here is the patch:
 
 void cfg80211_pmsr_wdev_down(struct wireless_dev *wdev)
 {
 	struct cfg80211_pmsr_request *req;
 	bool found = false;
 
 	spin_lock_bh(&wdev->pmsr_lock);
 	list_for_each_entry(req, &wdev->pmsr_list, list) {
 		found = true;
 		req->nl_portid = 0;
 	}
 	spin_unlock_bh(&wdev->pmsr_lock);
 
+	cancel_work_sync(&wdev->pmsr_free_wk);
 	if (found)
 		cfg80211_pmsr_process_abort(wdev);
 
 	WARN_ON(!list_empty(&wdev->pmsr_list));
 }
